name: Permission Slip
why_it_works: Many buyers want the thing but feel embarrassed, guilty or late. A permission statement removes the shame directly: it says the hesitation is normal and that starting now is allowed. Relief is a strong motivator, and the brand that gives it becomes the safe place to start.

hook.pattern: Start with 'You're allowed to...' followed by the exact thing the viewer feels guilty about.
examples: It's been {{time_gap}}? You're still allowed to come back.

variables.name: guilty_wish
variables.description: What the customer wants but feels bad about, lowercase verb phrase, 6 words or fewer
variables.example: book a cleaning after years away

variables.name: time_gap
variables.description: How long people typically stay away, lowercase, 3 words or fewer

variables.name: shame_thought
variables.example: they'll judge me the second I sit down

variables.name: what_actually_happens
variables.description: The calm truth of the first visit, starting with a capital letter, 10 words or fewer
variables.example: We ask two questions, then we just get started

variables.name: offer
variables.description: The low-pressure way in, lowercase, 5 words or fewer

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 photo of a person sitting in a car outside {{brand}}, hands on the wheel, hesitant expression, soft overcast light through the windshield
Vertical 9:16 gentle shot of a friendly staff member at {{brand}} greeting a client at the front desk, warm natural light, relaxed smiles, slow camera drift
Vertical 9:16 photo of the calm, clean waiting area at {{brand}}, plants, daylight, an empty comfortable chair facing camera

slides.headline: Your permission slip
slides.visual_prompt: Paper permission slip on a clipboard, pen beside it, soft daylight, {{brand}} colors

slides.headline: We know the thought
slides.visual_prompt: Person sitting in a parked car outside {{brand}}, hesitant, overcast light

slides.headline: Here's what really happens
slides.visual_prompt: Friendly staff greeting a client at the {{brand}} front desk, warm light

slides.headline: Nobody here keeps score
slides.body: Being away {{time_gap}} is common. We see it every week.
slides.visual_prompt: Calendar pages loosely fanned on a table, soft focus, calm tones

slides.headline: What to say at the desk
slides.body: Just this: "It's been {{time_gap}}." That's all we need to start.
slides.visual_prompt: Friendly front desk at {{brand}} with a small welcome card, soft daylight, nobody in frame

slides.headline: Signed. Now book it.
slides.visual_prompt: Signed permission slip with {{brand}} logo stamp, top-down

craft.notes: Quote the embarrassing thought in the customer's own words; if it feels too honest, it's right. Never lecture in the 'what actually happens' beat. The permission slip is a physical prop on the carousel so the metaphor is literal and shareable.

do_not: Turn permission into pressure ('so book now or else')
Shame people who wait, even jokingly
compliance: Dental and chiropractic: no promises of pain-free treatment or specific outcomes; describe the visit, not the result
Med spa and skincare: no before/after claims without 'individual results vary'; treatments must be described as performed by licensed providers where required
Fitness trainers: no weight-loss or body-change guarantees
